text:
A: Hello, can you hear me? I am Bożena.
B: Hi, yeah. Erm, I'm Bethany. Hi.
A: Hello, Bethany. Where do you live, if I can ask?
B: Basingstoke. You?
A: Southampton. In Bitterne.
B: Oh, I know Southampton a bit. I was at uni there, erm, for a year. I didn't finish, so.
A: Only a year? Well, that is still something. My son also changed his mind, and now he is in logistics near Reading, very happy. So what do you do now?
B: I'm on an IT service desk, at an insurance company. Fixing people's laptops, passwords, that sort of thing. It's alright. I like the people on the phone, mostly, even the cross ones.
A: The cross ones are not so bad, I think. I was pharmacy technician for eleven years, and some people come in very worried, very angry, but really they are frightened about medicine. You explain slowly and they are okay.
B: Yeah, that's exactly it. You just don't make them feel stupid.
A: Exactly, yes. Never make them feel stupid. You know, I saw your little cross in your photo. You go to church?
B: Erm, yeah, every few weeks. Church of England. I sort of sit at the back. Sorry, I saw yours too.
A: Yes, I go to the Polish parish most Sundays. Do you go to the same church since you are a child?
B: Erm, no, I switched a little while ago. It just felt a bit awkward at the old one, after some stuff. So. Yeah.
A: I understand. Sometimes a new place is better. When I came to England I was very lonely, and the parish is what helped me. The coffee morning, the ladies. I bake cakes for it now.
B: Oh, what do you bake?
A: What do I bake? Erm, sernik mostly, it is like a cheesecake, Polish style, baked. And poppy seed cake at Christmas. Do you bake?
B: A bit, yeah. My nan taught me a Victoria sponge. That's sort of my one thing really.
A: A Victoria sponge is very good thing to have. Your nan must be proud. You have family near you?
B: Yeah, my mum and dad are in Basingstoke. And I live with my partner, Dan, and our cat, Biscuit. He's a rescue.
A: Biscuit! This is a very good name for a cat. I have no cat, but I have two grandchildren, five and seven. I am knitting the little one a jumper with a dinosaur.
B: Aw, that's lovely. I'd love to be able to knit. I just do jigsaws and read, mostly.
A: Jigsaws are good for the head. My mother did jigsaws, she is eighty-four now, in Poland. Is this okay, I am talking a lot?
B: No, it's nice, honestly. I'm not very good at talking, so it's easier.
A: You are doing very well, Bethany. You talk like my daughter, quiet, but everything you say is—
